classes: authoritative: objects named by the archive manifest or a checkpoint reference, never candidates; rebuildable: retired index generations, rebuilt from the session catalog by the index worker
compatibility: objects written before reservations existed have no reservation and stay untouched; the archive acknowledge path, the index worker and the backup capture are unchanged
evidence_class: mocked: a SQLite catalog file and a local content addressed object folder stand in for the central database and the archive bucket; a deterministic hash embedder builds vectors, a fake clock drives expiry and grace, and a patched unlink stands in for a collector crash; no Pod, bucket or database runs

fixture_inputs.active_index: two embedding generations over the committed session, the newer one active and the older one retired
fixture_inputs.foreign_lookalike_object: a digest named object in a managed shard with no reservation, a stray root file and another domain's upload
fixture_inputs.newly_referenced_checkpoint: an abandoned upload that a task checkpoint references after collection claimed it
fixture_inputs.uncommitted_upload: an upload whose reservation expired past grace without an archive entry, beside one whose bytes never landed

interfaces: scripts.swarm_v2.garbage_collection.Reservations.reserve records an upload attempt with its digest and deadline before the bytes land, replays an identical reservation and refuses a conflicting reuse or a digest under collection

scripts.swarm_v2.garbage_collection.Reservations.commit releases the reservation and acknowledges the archive entry, which verifies the bytes; an unknown or collected upload, another digest or another domain is refused before any write
scripts.swarm_v2.garbage_collection.retire marks a registered non active index generation retired and keeps the first retirement time on a replay

scripts.swarm_v2.garbage_collection.collect deletes an object only with an expired reservation past grace held by the grant's domain alone, no archive manifest or checkpoint reference and bytes that hash to its name; it drops a retired generation past grace that is not active and took no work after retirement; with destructive off it is a read only inventory
metrics: garbage_collection_bytes counts reclaimed object bytes plus dropped vector text bytes; unsafe_delete_rejections counts unowned objects (no reservation, another domain's reservation, a name outside the managed shard layout) and objects whose bytes do not hash to their reserved name

outcomes.accepted: a reservation row or a retirement row in the catalog
outcomes.committed: deletions recorded by collect with committed true; inventory reports committed false
outcomes.externally_verified: none; no deployed catalog or bucket was collected
outcomes.observed: case outputs in the a, b and c result files from the focused fixture run

remaining_limitations: No live upload path reserves yet; the collector and spool do not write archive objects to this store, so collect reclaims only reservation backed uploads made through Reservations.
Checkpoint references come from a caller supplied set; there is no persisted checkpoint reference index in the catalog.

A reference added outside the catalog after collect's last reference read and before its unlink is not fenced; collect rereads references immediately before each unlink to narrow that window. A crash after an unlink and before its reservation rows are dropped leaves a claim with no bytes, and a later reference to that digest settles the claim as rebound although the bytes are gone; archive evidence reads still report the object missing.
No scheduler runs collect; an operator or job invokes it.
The grant principal is not checked against an operator role; the grant corpus scopes ownership, and the command line builds its grant from the domain an operator names.
rollback_rehearsal: B ran collect with destructive off and inside grace; the catalog, reservation and retirement rows, object files and vectors were unchanged, then a destructive collect reclaimed the same set the inventory listed
supported_versions: session catalog schema with archive_manifest and the index worker tables; upload_reservation and index_retirement tables are created on first use
